floor_history.headline: fable-blitz recon: v9 (per-arm 494D4 call dup + cross-jump remerge) is the proven chassis; sole residual = the offset web split (move s2,s0 in 493E4's delay slot) - cse/local-alloc forensics + wrap an

Solved v9's web split via recompute-inline (frame -32, no move copy, delay-nop restored); pure-C floor 10->8 (hoisted, capped); clean duplicated 0-path chassis at 13 with residual = 2 register assignm

frontier.hypothesis: The duplicated 0-path chassis (dup13_form.c, sandbox 13) reaches 0 by seating the per-arm ED6 read in v1 (read AFTER the ED2 multiply) so tbl keeps a0 uncontested; the only remaining gap is that sched1 hoists the ED6 load above the mult.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 list-scheduling picks the ready independent ED6 load before the ED2-dependent mult, keeping ED2 live in v1 at the ED6 read -> ED6 forced to a0, tbl to a1. Target schedules the final mult shift (sll v0,v0,1) into the j delay slot AFTER the ED6 read, freeing v1 for ED6.
frontier.next_probe: SCHEDULING/PERMUTER modality: reconstruct dup13_form.c, then (a) run the permuter to search the arm register/schedule space around it (residual is just 2 regs, base score ~13); or (b) find a byte-neutral C ordering that makes sched1 defer the ED6 load past the mult (e.g. PERM_* reorderings, or a delay-slot-filling structure per loop-note/scheduling rules). Verify tbl->a0 and ED6->v1 by reading the sandbox asm.

frontier.hypothesis: If scheduling cannot seat ED6 in v1, the duplicated chassis may still close via a different but byte-identical register partition, or the residual is a genuine sched1 fork-tie needing the endgame-lock disposition.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc qty priority + sched1 launch timing determine the a0/a1/v1 seats; the marionation evidence shows these ties are C-reachable but sometimes only via non-structural levers.
frontier.next_probe: After the permuter pass, if still 13 with the ED6-hoist surviving, take a standalone cc1 -da of dup13_form.c and read base.i.sched/.greg to confirm whether the ED6 load's sched1 priority can be lowered by any C ordering; escalate only if every scheduling/permuter axis is measured dead.
